record.program_name: Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Rounds 1 to 7, County and Mendocino County Homeless Services CoC CA-509
record.administering_agency: Mendocino County Social Services (administrative entity for CA-509; Veronica Wilson, (707) 468-7071)
record.typical_award_size: HHAP-6 joint regional application for $1,826,480.60 (County $883,203.78 plus CoC $943,276.82), resolution adopted April 7, 2026, agreement through June 30, 2029; prior rounds: HHAP-1 $924,734.12 (CoC) and $856,699.99 (County), HHAP-2 $437,551 and $391,634, HHAP-3 $567,869.71 initial plus $1,703,609.13 remainder. HHAP-7 preliminary: County $811,781.46, CoC $869,765.85. Key Action 1 of the regional plan is to fully fund existing interim housing (Ford Street Project, Mendocino Coast Hospitality Center, Redwood Community Services, Project Sanctuary) through June 30, 2029; RFP 004-26 (due February 17, 2026) solicited shelter operators to obligate HHAP-6 and prior-round balances.
record.affordability_requirement: Homeless and at-risk households; 10% youth set-aside; Coordinated Entry referrals.
record.next_deadline: No local capital NOFA; the CoC states it will provide letters of support and may allocate future HHAP to new interim or affordable units. HHAP-7 allocations are preliminary for FY 2026-27.
record.layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. HHAP is fully absorbed by shelter operations; its relevance to a developer is a CoC letter of support and possible operating subsidy for PSH units referred through Coordinated Entry. Source is the April 7, 2026 Board item on Granicus Ideas with the HHAP-6 regional application attached.
eligible_project_detail: permanent housing operating support (eligible; not funded locally)

record.program_name: Ukiah Housing Trust Fund (UHTF) NOFA, funded with PLHA, Prohousing Incentive Pilot (PIP) and housing successor funds
record.administering_agency: City of Ukiah Community Development Department, Housing Services Division (Housing and Grants Manager, housing@cityofukiah.com, 707-463-6708)
record.typical_award_size: Most recent round: June 10, 2024 NOFA for about $1,000,000 to acquire infill parcels for affordable housing, combining a $455,000 Prohousing Incentive Pilot award (October 2023) with up to $617,000 of the City's 2019-2022 PLHA allocation. Loans at 0 to 3% simple interest, 55-year term, repaid from residual cash flow after operating costs, senior debt, reserves and deferred developer fee; due on sale or refinance. Commitments last 24 months from Council approval (one-year extension possible). Earlier UHTF capital came from former RDA housing bond proceeds; the 2019 Housing Element notes a $500,000 NOFA in 2018. Acorn Valley Plaza (DANCO, 74 units, opened March 2025) was built with UHTF funds.
record.per_unit_cap: None published; sized as gap funding after all other sources.
record.affordability_requirement: Units affordable at or below 60%, 80% or 120% AMI with a recorded 55-year rent or resale covenant; bonus points for units at 0 to 30% AMI. Funding-source rules (PLHA, PIP) add restrictions.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency. The 2024 round closed July 8, 2024 and no newer NOFA is posted on the Housing Services page as of 2026-11-08. Projects must deploy UHTF funds and start construction within two years of award.
record.layering_notes: Ukiah is the only priority city in Mendocino County with a standing local trust fund and was the first rural Northern California city with a Prohousing Designation (April 2023), which earns state Prohousing points on AHSC, IIG and similar applications. The 2024 round targeted parcels in TCAC High and Highest Resource areas and favored scattered-site or non-traditional infill. The Housing Element says the fund exists partly to supply local match points for tax credit applications. Stacks with County HOME program income (about $351,767, for example the Marigold Villas request in Ukiah) and the City's own state HOME awards; County PLHA is a separate formula pool. Local public funds trigger state prevailing wage under Labor Code 1720.
record.cycle_notes: irregular; issued when state funds are awarded

record.program_name: Ukiah Housing Successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF)
record.administering_agency: City of Ukiah as Housing Successor to the former Ukiah Redevelopment Agency (Housing Services Division)
record.typical_award_size: Former RDA housing bond proceeds deposited in the LMIHAF and used to seed the Ukiah Housing Trust Fund in 2017. The City Council authorized $500,000 for affordable housing activities in FY 2019-20 (2019 Housing Element). Current balance not published on the City site; check the annual Housing Successor report (Health and Safety Code 34176.1).
record.affordability_requirement: At least two-thirds of LMIHAF spending must serve households at or below 60% AMI (Mendocino County); eligible uses include rental rehab, acquisition-rehab and new construction.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency; funds are offered through Ukiah Housing Trust Fund rounds rather than a separate application.
record.layering_notes: Treat as part of the UHTF capital stack, not a separate window. Housing successor income targeting (two-thirds at 60% AMI or below) is stricter than the UHTF NOFA's 120% AMI ceiling, so the City will steer LMIHAF dollars to lower-income units. Balance and five-year expenditure deadlines should be confirmed from the City's latest Housing Successor annual report, which was not located on the City site this pass. Source is the adopted 2019-2027 Housing Element hosted by HCD.

record.program_name: Housing Mendocino Coast community land trust partnership (ARPA housing funds and PLHA), 251 S. Franklin Street
record.administering_agency: City of Fort Bragg City Manager's Office with Housing Mendocino Coast (501(c)(3) community land trust)
record.typical_award_size: Council obligated $800,000 in ARPA funds to housing (Resolution 4859-2024); about $50,000 went to the Prohousing Designation application. June 22, 2026 staff recommended $350,000 of remaining ARPA housing funds for HMC's acquisition of 251 S. Franklin Street (about 1 acre, 12 to 13 workforce units) and working capital, under an MOU to be drafted in summer 2026. HMC reports about $1.39 million in existing funding. The City previously used SB 2, LEAP, REAP and PLHA funds to form HMC.
record.affordability_requirement: Households up to 120% AMI; CLT ground lease (typically 99 years) with resale restrictions; possible priority for City employees and local workforce.
record.next_deadline: MOU and funding documents were to be prepared in summer 2026; ARPA funds must be expended by December 31, 2026 under federal rules, so verify status with the City Manager.
record.layering_notes: Not a general NOFA; the City routes funds to its incubated CLT. Useful as a land and ownership partner for small workforce projects rather than a gap lender for tax credit rentals. The staff report states $300,000 in the recommendation and $350,000 in the discussion; confirm the final amount. Fort Bragg also references a Prohousing Designation application funded with ARPA; designation status was not confirmed this pass.

record.program_name: Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Rounds 1 to 7 and other CoC-administered funds, Merced City and County CoC CA-520
record.administering_agency: Merced County Human Services Agency (Collaborative Applicant and Administrative Entity for the Merced City and County Continuum of Care; collabapp@countyofmerced.com)
record.typical_award_size: HHAP-6 allocations: Merced County $955,092.45 and Merced County CoC $1,020,055.16; HHAP-7 preliminary: County $915,168.72, CoC $980,537.91. CoC-administered rounds: HHAP-1 $716,227.19, HHAP-2 $338,893 (rapid rehousing $171,115, D Street Shelter operating subsidy $100,000, HMIS and CES $16,944), HHAP-3 $909,988.45, HHAP-4 $1,136,537.22 ($400,000 unobligated at reporting); the CoC also managed HHIP $1,260,500, ESG $2,452,084, ESG-CV $3,170,800, HEAP $1,338,104.53, CESH $1,637,863 and HUD CoC grants $6,433,137, a total of $19,950,660.47 across 14 sources from FY 2016-17 to FY 2023-24. The state dashboard reports $4 million of HHAP rounds 1 to 5 went directly to Merced County.
record.affordability_requirement: Homeless and at-risk households; 10% youth set-aside; Coordinated Entry referrals; 2024 Regionally Coordinated Homelessness Action Plan with the City of Merced.
record.next_deadline: No local capital NOFA; the CoC's 2024 regional plan lists CDBG, HOME, Homekey, PLHA, MHP and REAP as sources it will pursue for dedicated affordable units, led by local jurisdictions. HHAP-7 allocations are preliminary for FY 2026-27.
record.layering_notes: Merced County has no County housing finance program: the Community and Economic Development Department handles planning and the Housing Element, the Human Services Agency is Collaborative Applicant and Administrative Entity for the Merced City and County Continuum of Care (CA-520) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, and the Housing Authority of the County of Merced (HACM) is the countywide PHA. The County is a non-entitlement jurisdiction for CDBG and HOME, has no housing trust fund, inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee or fee waiver, and Measure V (MCAG half-cent sales tax) is transportation only. The City of Merced is the entitlement jurisdiction with PLHA and Homekey awards (Pass 3). countyofmerced.com is Cloudflare-blocked to automated access (pages, DocumentCenter and AgendaCenter), so records were built from HCD tables and letters, mercedcoc.org reports, merced-pha.com, gocodebook (County Code Title 18) and press coverage; County documents are flagged for confirmation. HHAP in Merced funds rapid rehousing and the D Street Shelter rather than capital; Homekey units in the region (1213 V Street, 95 units; R Street, 21 veteran PSH units) are City of Merced projects. A PSH developer should seek a CoC letter of support and Coordinated Entry referrals. Source is the Merced CoC Grants and Funding Report (FY 2016-17 to FY 2023-24) on mercedcoc.org; HHAP-6 and HHAP-7 figures from HCD allocation tables.
eligible_project_detail: dedicated affordable housing units with rapid rehousing assistance (regional plan action 1a.3)

record.program_name: City of Merced Density Bonus Ordinance (Merced Municipal Code Title 20) and 2024-2032 Housing Element incentives (Programs 2, 6 and 7: fee deferrals, reductions or waivers; 50% senior bonus; UC Merced Student Housing Plan)
record.administering_agency: City of Merced Development Services Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. The ordinance was adopted in 2005 and amended in 2016; it caps the bonus at 35% and lags current state law, which the City commits to fix. The Housing Element commits to: amend the Zoning Code by July 2026 to allow a 50% bonus for senior housing with at least 50% very low income units; offer expedited processing and fee deferrals, reductions or waivers for affordable units on large inventory sites (with extra incentives by July 2028 if needed); scope a UC Merced Student Housing Plan; and require 5% affordable housing plans in annexations around UC Merced.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds; senior enhancement requires at least 50% very low income units.
record.next_deadline: Available at entitlement, no deadline. The 6th Cycle Housing Element went to the Planning Commission in April 2026 (Resolution 4181), and Ordinance 2594 (RHNA rezones) had its second reading in July 2026. Verify whether the density bonus update and senior bonus amendment have been adopted.
record.layering_notes: Merced has no inclusionary ordinance or commercial linkage fee, and the fee deferrals and waivers are Housing Element commitments, not an adopted program. Fund 1020 is the practical way to cover fees today. The UC Merced items are planning commitments, not funding. Merced does not appear to be a Prohousing jurisdiction; the HCD list page returned 404 this pass, so this was not confirmed. The code chapter was not opened directly: zoneomics has Title 20, but the density bonus section was not isolated. The Housing Element was read as a City Legistar attachment.

record.program_name: Monterey County Housing Trust Fund (MCHTF) loans for affordable rental development
record.administering_agency: Monterey County Housing and Community Development Department
record.typical_award_size: Established May 17, 2022 (Resolution 22-100) to replace redevelopment set-aside; by April 2023 the County had committed $10,033,984 of local cash, land assets and PLHA to capitalize it, including about $420,000 of PLHA delegated by Carmel-by-the-Sea, Greenfield and Soledad plus about $289,000 a year from those cities' later allocations. Loans: Greenfield Commons (EAH Housing, 100 units, Greenfield) $1,929,046 ($1,028,833 trust fund plus $900,213 PLHA) approved March 2023 and increased by $550,000 trust fund plus $9,982 PLHA on December 22, 2025 for cost overruns; Lightfighter Village (EAH and Veterans Transition Center, 71 units, Marina) $500,115. Loan origination fee corrected to 0.5%. The County applied to the state Local Housing Trust Fund matching program in 2022 (unsuccessful) and 2023 (up to $5 million match on $3,544,645 eligible local funds); a 2024 Board referral explored using 1220 Natividad Road to recapitalize the fund.
record.per_unit_cap: Not published; awards of $500,000 to $2.5 million per project (about $5,000 to $25,000 per unit).
record.affordability_requirement: Lower income rental housing with 55-year County regulatory agreements; LHTF rules (3% simple maximum, predevelopment, acquisition, construction and permanent loans) when matched by state funds.
record.next_deadline: No standing NOFA; awards have gone by Board resolution to projects identified in the County's LHTF application. Contact HCD housing staff about trust fund and PLHA availability for 2027 tax credit applications; the pending inclusionary fee restructuring is intended to feed this fund.
record.layering_notes: Monterey County's Housing and Community Development Department (HCD, Craig Spencer, Director; Darby Marshall, Housing Program Manager) runs the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, the Monterey County Housing Trust Fund, PLHA, the Urban County CDBG and HOME programs and County land dispositions; the County Administrative Office Homelessness Strategies and Initiatives Division (CAO-HSI) runs HHAP and the SHARE Center; the Health Department Behavioral Health Bureau holds BHSA; the Coalition of Homeless Services Providers leads the CoC (CA-506, shared with San Benito); and the Housing Authority of the County of Monterey (HACM) and its Development Corporation supply vouchers and develop housing. Salinas, Monterey, Seaside and other entitlement cities run their own programs (Pass 3). countyofmonterey.gov blocks automated access (pages and documents), so records were built from the Legistar web API client 'monterey' and its Granicus attachments, hamonterey.org, chsp.org, zoneomics and HCD tables. The trust fund is the County's gap lender of record but is thinly capitalized (two projects to date); its future depends on inclusionary in-lieu fee revenue and PLHA delegations from small cities. Source is the December 22, 2025 Board item (Legistar file 26-009) with the Greenfield Commons loan resolutions; establishment and LHTF history from files RES 22-100 and RES 23-073.
record.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: Board report 26-009 confirms Greenfield Commons $1,929,046 ($1,028,833 trust fund plus $900,213 PLHA), increase up to $550,000 trust fund plus $9,982 PLHA, Lightfighter Village $500,115, origination fee corrected to 0.5%, 55-year 3% residual receipts loans. The item was introduced December 22, 2025 and heard January 13, 2026 (not decided December 22). The report also says EAH is repaying the Lightfighter loan and the repayment was recycled into Greenfield Commons, and describes the trust fund as authorized in November 2022. prevailing_wage_trigger true is uncited.

record.program_name: County land for affordable housing: 855 East Laurel Drive, Salinas (Eden Housing) and SHARE Center reconfiguration

record.next_deadline: Eden Housing is assembling local funding (County trust fund and PLHA, City of Salinas) before CTCAC applications; no other County sites are currently offered. record.program_name: Salinas Local Housing Trust Fund (Fund 2603) and Multifamily Housing NOFA gap financing (FY 2025-26 round, Resolution 23358)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division (City Council sits as the Salinas LHTF Board of Directors)
record.typical_award_size: The June 24, 2025 Multifamily Housing NOFA offered about $8 million of gap financing; five proposals requested $17,981,000 and four were conditionally committed on November 18, 2025 (Resolution 23358) for $8,460,220: Vista de la Terraza rehabilitation (CHISPA, 40 units) $960,000 (CDBG $400,000, HOME $560,000); Saint George Apartments (CHISPA, 36 senior units) $3,017,699 including $1,432,000 LHTF, $397,000 HOME, $543,699 PLHA and $645,000 PLHA for land; Casentini Street Family Apartments (HACM and Milestone Housing, 88 units plus daycare) $3,837,000 ($570,000 LHTF, $3,267,000 HOME); Republic Cafe (City-owned, Chinatown) $1,290,521 LHTF. The Local Housing Trust Fund was established May 2, 2023; HCD awarded $3,807,248 in January 2024 against a $4,526,562 local match, and the City applied again in September 2024 for $1.5 million with a General Fund match of about $1.5 million. HSA, PLHA and PIP funds supply at least $100,000 a year of ongoing trust fund revenue.
record.per_unit_cap: None published; awards sized to the gap shown in the applicant pro forma.
record.affordability_requirement: LHTF-funded units restricted to 60% AMI or below (extremely low, very low and low income) under the City's LHTF program design; federal HOME and CDBG layers carry their own rent and income limits; 55-year covenants used on City loans.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The October 20, 2026 HLUC update (file 26-494) reports only on the four FY 2025-26 awards (NEPA and covenants pending; Casentini expects its tax credit result in November 2026; a Republic Cafe development partner RFP is planned by the end of 2026) and announces no new Multifamily NOFA. The City keeps an open application for shovel-ready HOME projects; contact the CDD Housing Division, (831) 758-7334.
record.layering_notes: Largest city-controlled pool in Monterey County. Stacks City HOME, CDBG, LHTF, PLHA and HSA money into one commitment that is then paired with 9% or 4% tax credits (Casentini applied September 8, 2026; Saint George applies after the City commitment). The County's Monterey County Housing Trust Fund (county record) is a separate pool that has not lent inside Salinas; County PLHA is also separate from the City's own PLHA (Salinas is a direct PLHA entitlement, see City PLHA record). The County-owned 855 East Laurel Drive Eden Housing project (county record) is in Salinas and may seek City gap funds in a future round. Blocked: cityofsalinas.org and salinas.gov return 403 to scripts; all material was read from the Salinas Legistar web API and legistar2.granicus.com attachments (staff report of October 20, 2026, Legistar file 26-494, and the September 10, 2024 LHTF staff report, file 24-480).
record.cycle_notes: Multifamily Housing NOFA last released June 24, 2025 (about $8 million; $8,460,220 conditionally committed November 18, 2025 by Resolution 23358). No FY 2026-27 or later NOFA found in Salinas Legistar items through November 8, 2026. Rounds have been issued when HOME, LHTF, PLHA and HSA balances accumulate rather than on a fixed annual date.

record.program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), City of Salinas five-year plan (direct entitlement)
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Standard Agreement with HCD (June 2021) for up to $6,041,082 over the first five years; Fund 2951 Financial Assistance - Multi Family Housing appropriation $3,322,776.95 as of November 2024. Fourth plan amendment (November 19, 2024) set years three to five at 41% to 55% affordable housing development, 14% ADU production in year three, 40% homeownership in years three to five and 5% administration, and allocated $390,000 to CHISPA for three ADUs (138 Carr Avenue, 615 and 617 Fremont Street, rented up to moderate income) and $645,000 to CHISPA for land at 98 Kip Drive for 36 senior units. Earlier uses: Parkside Manor (2021), Fairview (Salinas Inn) Homekey acquisition with HACM ($2,500,000 of PLHA and PIP in 2025, 45 PSH units), SHARE Center homeless services. In January 2026 Council approved a PLHA-funded Mortgage Down Payment Assistance Program (deferred loans up to 150% AMI).
record.per_unit_cap: None stated; ADU awards averaged $130,000 per unit.
record.affordability_requirement: PLHA rules: rental development for extremely low to moderate income, ADUs up to moderate income, homeownership up to 150% AMI; City covenants recorded on assisted properties.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Multifamily PLHA dollars are committed through the City's Multifamily NOFA (Saint George Apartments $543,699 plus $645,000 for land) and no new NOFA has been announced. The PLHA-funded First Time Homebuyer Mortgage Down Payment Assistance Program ($1.3 million, deferred loans up to $125,000 or 17% of price, 3% interest, 30-year term, about ten loans) was projected to launch in November 2026.
record.layering_notes: Salinas receives its own PLHA formula allocation and does not share in the County PLHA plan (county record), which covers the unincorporated area plus Carmel-by-the-Sea, Greenfield and Soledad. PLHA pays land and predevelopment costs that HOME cannot (Saint George land $645,000), so it is usually the first City dollar in before a HOME or LHTF commitment. PLHA was also used as the local operating match for the Fairview Homekey PSH site now owned by HACM. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 24-570, November 19, 2024) because the City website blocks scripts.
record.cycle_notes: PLHA plan amendments require a 10-day public notice and Council hearing. Developer access to PLHA for rental projects is through the City's periodic Multifamily NOFA (last released June 24, 2025). The January 27, 2026 down payment program (HCD approved guidelines February 10, 2026) is a homebuyer program, not a developer funding round.

record.program_name: Housing Successor Agency (former Salinas Redevelopment Agency) Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund loans
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas as Housing Successor Agency; Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Gap loans from the HSA Affordable Housing fund awarded through the City's annual housing NOFA. Example: $500,000 at 0% for 55 years to Sun Rose Housing, LLC (Interim, Inc.) for the 11-unit Sun Rose Apartments at 439 Soledad Street (8-bed transitional unit plus 9 permanent supportive units), approved December 6, 2022 after an $800,000 construction cost gap; the same site earlier received an $80,000 RDA grant (2000) and $500,000 CDBG (2021). HSA funds are also pledged as part of the $100,000 a year ongoing revenue for the Salinas Local Housing Trust Fund.
record.affordability_requirement: Very low and low income (HSA law caps use at 80% AMI with at least 30% of expenditures for extremely low income over five-year periods); 55-year deed restrictions on assisted projects.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. HSA gap loans are awarded through the City's periodic housing NOFA (the Sun Rose loan came from the February 2022 NOFA; the most recent Multifamily NOFA opened June 24, 2025) and no new NOFA was announced in Salinas Legistar items through November 8, 2026.
record.layering_notes: The former RDA housing set-aside is the most flexible local layer (no NEPA, 0% long-term loans) and has been used to close inflation gaps on projects that already hold CDBG or HOME. Combine with Monterey County Behavioral Health (MCHOME program) services funding for PSH, and with County HHAP for operating support (county records). Fund balance was not published in the documents opened; confirm with the Housing Division before underwriting. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 22-560, December 6, 2022 staff report) because the City website blocks scripts.
record.cycle_notes: HSA Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund money is offered through the City's housing NOFA alongside HOME, CDBG, LHTF and PLHA when balances allow, not on a fixed annual date. Fund balance is reported in the annual Housing Successor report filed with the Housing Element APR.

record.program_name: Prohousing Designation and Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) awards, Fund 2958
record.administering_agency: City of Salinas Community Development Department, Housing and Community Development Division
record.typical_award_size: Salinas holds an HCD Prohousing Designation (application authorized November 29, 2022). PIP Round 1 award $1,650,000 funded an Affordable Housing Program and a First Time Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance Program; Rounds 2 and 3 applications (2024) were not funded; the Round 4 application for $1,250,000 (authorized March 24, 2026, proposing $1,000,000 for the City-owned El Rey Motel and $250,000 for down payment assistance) was also not funded: HCD's Round 4 awardee list ($11,299,410.78 total) shows Salinas (PDP score 58) unfunded and deprioritized because it received a prior-round award. PIP funds were also matched with PLHA ($2,500,000 combined) for HACM's Fairview Homekey acquisition in 2025. Round 5 offers about $8 million statewide.
record.affordability_requirement: PIP allows rapid rehousing, rental assistance, shelters, new construction, rehabilitation and preservation of permanent and transitional housing, and homeownership assistance up to 150% AMI.
record.next_deadline: PIP Round 5 applications due March 31, 2027 (NOFA released October 13, 2026; awards expected June 2027). Jurisdictions funded in earlier rounds, including Salinas, are funded only after all previously unfunded eligible applicants receive awards.
record.layering_notes: The designation is a scoring layer for developers applying to state programs for Salinas sites, and PIP money has been redeployed locally to PSH acquisitions and down payment assistance. Pairs with the City-County MOU to pursue Encampment Resolution Funds Round 5 for the El Rey Motel. No other Monterey County priority city held the designation in the documents opened; Marina submitted a draft application in August 2025 and Soledad states it is pursuing one. Read through the Salinas Legistar API (file 26-111, March 24, 2026 staff report).
record.cycle_notes: HCD PIP runs roughly annual rounds. Round 4 NOFA September 30, 2025, applications due March 31, 2026, Salinas not funded. Round 5 NOFA October 13, 2026, applications due March 31, 2027, Prohousing Designation required by March 31, 2027, awards June 2027.

record.program_name: Affordable Housing Requirements (Zoning Code Chapter 17.32, 20% inclusionary), in-lieu fund and Campus Town Affordable Housing Agreement
record.administering_agency: City of Seaside Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Every residential development and condominium conversion must provide at least 20% of units as inclusionary units for moderate, low and very low income households (first third low, second third very low), calculated before any density bonus; equivalents allow one very low unit to count as two moderate units and one low unit as 1.5. Affordability 40 years for rental and for each sale of ownership units. Alternatives (17.32.060): off-site units, land dedication, or any combination of on-site, off-site, in-lieu fees and land dedication equal to the on-site cost. Exemptions: government-built housing, second units, replacement after disaster. The fifth cycle Housing Element reported about $2.6 million in the inclusionary in-lieu fund as of 2017, used for grants to nonprofits. Campus Town (KB Bakewell, Fort Ord, 1,485 units) carries an Affordable Housing Agreement for 225 affordable units (74 very low, 78 low, 73 moderate), equivalent to 350 units, with 161 affordable units in Phase 1 including off-site very low and low income units and land dedicated for a nonprofit rental project.
record.affordability_requirement: Very low (50% AMI), low (80%) and moderate (120%) households; 40-year covenants; tenants may be drawn from the HACM Section 8 waiting list.
record.next_deadline: Applies at tentative map, use permit or building permit. Campus Town Phase 1 final map approved and ground broken in 2025; the City bought a 1.62-acre MST parcel in Campus Town in December 2025 and streamlined Campus Town review in February 2026. The 2023-2031 Housing Element (draft May 2023) and Seaside 2040 General Plan were still being finalized in the documents opened.
record.layering_notes: Seaside's 20% requirement with no ten-unit threshold is the broadest in the county, but the code sets no fee schedule; in-lieu payments are negotiated case by case. The in-lieu fund (about $2.6 million in 2017, about $9 million across two restricted housing funds in 2018 per candidate statements, unverified) plus former RDA successor agency land in the Long Range Property Management Plan are the City's local layers for a nonprofit partner on the Campus Town dedication site or Seaside East. Blocked: ci.seaside.ca.us AgendaCenter is JavaScript-only and the CivicClerk portal only lists meetings from October 2026; code text read on the zoneomics mirror, program history from the fifth cycle Housing Element PDF on hcd.ca.gov. Confirm the current fund balance and any 2024-2026 fee resolution with Planning.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: code text for 17.32.020 through 17.32.090 matches (20%, first third low and second third very low, density bonus units excluded, VL=2 and L=1.5 moderate equivalents, 40-year terms, exemptions, alternatives, Section 8 waiting list option). Prevailing wage false is uncited; no rule was cited for an inclusionary requirement.

record.program_name: PLHA delegated to Monterey County and City request for the $1.68 million affordable owner-occupied workforce housing (AOWH) set-aside for a moderate income land purchase
record.administering_agency: City of Soledad (requesting agency) with Monterey County Housing and Community Development Department (Darby Marshall, Housing Program Manager, (831) 755-5391)
record.typical_award_size: Soledad delegated its 2019-2023 PLHA allocation to the County in 2024 (with Carmel-by-the-Sea and Greenfield, adding about $1.74 million to the County plan). On March 16, 2026 the County Health, Housing, Homelessness and Human Services Committee considered Soledad's request to use the County's reserved AOWH funds, about $1,680,063, to buy land in Soledad for homes sold to moderate income households under a 45-year resale restriction, with the City selecting a developer; staff would amend the County PLHA plan with HCD and memorialize the City's obligations. The City receives RHNA credit for the units.
record.affordability_requirement: Moderate income (up to 120% AMI) owner-occupied units with 45-year deed and resale restrictions under PLHA AOWH rules.
record.next_deadline: unknown, verify with agency. Committee recommendation to the Board of Supervisors was pending in spring 2026; the County's PLHA balance was $1,191,927 in September 2026 (county record) so the AOWH reserve may already be partly committed.
record.layering_notes: This is a County-controlled dollar (see county PLHA record) directed to a Soledad project; it would pair with Soledad's inclusionary Affordable Housing Fund and a developer's for-sale product in the Miramonte or Miravale areas. Soledad's own 2024-2028 PLHA allocations also flow to the County (about $289,000 a year across the three delegating cities). The Monterey County Housing Trust Fund (county record) has lent in Greenfield and Marina but not yet Soledad. Read through the Monterey County Legistar web API and the staff report PDF (file 26-261) because cityofsoledad.gov could not be reached.
record.audit_note: Spot check Nov 9, 2026: committee report 26-261 (introduced March 16, 2026, hearing dated March 26, 2026) confirms the 2024 delegation by Carmel-by-the-Sea, Greenfield and Soledad, the $1,680,063 AOWH reserve, the moderate-income for-sale land purchase with 45-year resale restriction, plan amendment with HCD and RHNA credit to the City. No later Board of Supervisors item on the Soledad request was found in the Legistar API through November 2026. prevailing_wage_trigger true is uncited.

record.program_name: City land for the Soledad homeless youth housing campus (federal Community Project Funding grant B-22-CP-CA-0157, $2 million) and Prohousing Designation pursuit
record.administering_agency: City of Soledad with Monterey County Housing and Community Development Department, Housing Authority of the County of Monterey and CHISPA
record.typical_award_size: The County holds a $2 million HUD Community Project Funding grant (2022, sponsored by Senator Padilla) for a south county housing campus for unhoused parenting youth aged 18 to 24. The City bought a lot next to Vosti Park on Monterey Street with City funds, is demolishing the dilapidated house and remediating the site, and will sell the site to the project using CPF funds; CHISPA will install four to six two-bedroom manufactured homes as permanent supportive housing owned and managed by HACM, with a City, County and HACM services financing plan. Status report to the County 4HS Committee March 26, 2026 (file 26-251). The City's housing web page also states Soledad is pursuing an HCD Prohousing Designation (page not reachable this pass).
record.per_unit_cap: About $333,000 to $500,000 per unit of CPF grant depending on final unit count.
record.affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing for transition-age parenting youth experiencing homelessness (extremely low income), consistent with CPF grant terms.
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; single earmarked project. NEPA review and site transfer pending in 2026.
record.layering_notes: Illustrates Soledad's model: city-owned land plus County-held grants (CPF, HHAP youth set-aside in the county HHAP record) and HACM ownership. The County HHAP-6 plan includes $277,969.56 for a permanent supportive housing project with a city partner with a youth set-aside, which likely attaches to this campus. Prohousing Designation would add state scoring points but was not confirmed because cityofsoledad.gov timed out and refused connections on every attempt (fetch helper, WebFetch and curl). Read through the Monterey County Legistar web API and staff report PDF.
